headline: Epoch AI's index finds that China's best AI models have trailed the US frontier by an average of seven months since 2023, with the gap ranging from four to fourteen months.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 5: useful measure, but the article's date for the Epoch analysis is unclear and it blends older data with commentary.
importance_line: Policymakers weighing chip export controls and companies choosing between US closed and Chinese open models are affected, but the figures come from one index and mix several studies, and no Chinese model has yet matched OpenAI's o3.
summary: Startup Fortune reports, citing the research group Epoch AI, that Chinese AI models have trailed the US frontier by an average of seven months since 2023, within a range of four to fourteen months, and that this gap closely matches the gap between open-weight models (whose files are public) and closed ones. The outlet also cites a Mozilla-backed analysis putting the gap near 4.4 months with Chinese open models up to five times cheaper per task, and questions whether US export controls still make sense, an opinion rather than a finding.
notes: Epoch AI's own page was not read; figures are as relayed by Startup Fortune. The article does not date the Epoch analysis.
